title: Quiz: The Pure Birth Process — Yule Model

questions.text: In the Yule process, the birth rate when the population is n is:
options: nλ (proportional to the current population size)
questions.explanation: The defining property of the Yule process is λₙ = nλ. Each individual reproduces independently at rate λ, so the total rate when there are n individuals is nλ. This is what distinguishes it from the Poisson process (constant rate λ).

questions.text: The ODE P_j'(t) = −jλP_j(t) arises in the Yule process because:
options: The process has no death events
Starting at population j, the only possible event is a birth that moves the process to state j+1, so the only way to leave state j is through that single birth event
j individuals each die at rate λ, reducing the population
The process is at j and receives j immigrants per unit time
questions.explanation: When n = j (the starting state), the term (n−1)λP_{n−1}(t) = (j−1)λP_{j−1}(t) = 0 because P_{j−1}(0) = 0 and the pure birth process cannot descend from j to j−1. So only the outflow term −jλP_j(t) remains, reflecting that a birth occurs at total rate jλ and takes the process out of state j.

questions.text: The population size X(t) in a Yule process starting at j = 1 follows a geometric distribution with parameter p = e^{−λt}.
questions.explanation: With j = 1, the general formula P_n(t) = C(n−1, 0) e^{−λt}(1−e^{−λt})^{n−1} simplifies to (1−e^{−λt})^{n−1} × e^{−λt}, which is the Geometric(p) PMF with p = e^{−λt}. The negative binomial NegBin(j=1, p) is the geometric distribution.

options: The population grows linearly at rate jλ
The population doubles at a constant absolute rate
The expected population grows exponentially with intrinsic rate λ
The population size is normally distributed around je^{λt}
questions.explanation: je^{λt} is an exponential function of t with rate constant λ. Exponential growth means the per-capita rate of increase is constant at λ, not that the absolute increment is constant (linear) or that the distribution is normal. The doubling time is ln(2)/λ.

questions.text: In the Yule process, increasing λ increases both the mean and the variance of X(t) at any fixed time t > 0.
questions.explanation: E[X(t)] = je^{λt} and Var[X(t)] = je^{λt}(e^{λt}−1). Both are strictly increasing functions of λ for t > 0. A faster birth rate produces a larger expected population and wider spread around that mean.
